Subject: Access delegation mapping request and SCIM attributes

Hi Clara —

Thanks for sending the SIG follow-up. A couple of quick clarifying asks from our side on the access delegation section so we can produce a crisp evidence package:

- Do you provision users into Acme via a single IdP tenant, or do you use multiple IdP tenants for different business units? That affects how we demonstrate group-to-role mapping.
- Which roles in your IAM map to an elevated "Application Admin" vs "Support Engineer" vs "Read-only"? If you can attach a list (group names or role IDs) we’ll map them into our SCIM template.
- For temporary access (breakglass/devops), do you expect time-bound SCIM groups or manual requests through your ticketing system?

I attached a small template (scim-role-mapping-template.csv) and a simple access diagram to show how we typically represent role scoping for SIG deliverables. If you can drop your SCIM attribute export into a reply, Soojin will map it to our recommended least-privilege role set and call out any gaps.

Proposed next steps:
1) You send the SCIM attribute export (group names + member emails) — ideally by EOD Wed PST
2) Soojin and Marcus will produce a mapping + short evidence bundle (screenshots + log extract) within 48 hours
3) We can schedule a 30-min sync to review and sign off — calendar link below

Attachments: scim-role-mapping-template.csv (CSV), access-diagram.png (PNG)

Thanks —

Subject: Re: Access delegation mapping request and SCIM attributes

Hi Clara —

Thanks for the export. I pulled the sheet into the template and sketched a recommended mapping for Acme’s groups. High-level summary below and a few evidence notes we can include in the SIG response.

Mapping highlights (excerpt):
- Okta group: acme-app-admin -> Redwood role: tenant_admin (access: settings, audit-logs)
- Okta group: acme-support -> Redwood role: support_engineer (access: user troubleshooting, session traces)
- Okta group: acme-sre -> Redwood role: infra_operator (access: runtime metrics, not tenant config)

Least-privilege controls we enforce by default:
- No role grants billing or tenant-delete rights unless explicitly requested and approved by an enterprise admin (we record approvals in the activity audit).
- SCIM sync only writes membership changes; it does not auto-promote permissions beyond the pre-defined role mapping table.
- MFA: enforced at IdP level; Redwood validates IdP assertion for AAL2+ and rejects sessions lacking MFA assertion for elevated flows.

Evidence we will bundle:
1) Mapping CSV populated for Acme (attached back to this thread)
2) SCIM provisioning logs (scrubbed) and a screenshot of successful patch response from our provisioning endpoint
3) A short video GIF showing group assignment -> SSO login -> role propagation in the Console (we will provide a Drive link)

Notes / questions:
- For breakglass groups: if you can share one ticket reference (or give us a time-window) we can pull the SCIM delta and show the ephemeral membership change in the logs.
- For the "App Admin" concern: we will explicitly mark which Console permissions are included in tenant_admin vs support_engineer and create a one-page permission matrix for sign-off.

Attachments: scim-provisioning-screenshots.pdf

--
